title: DryerJack Roof Installation
description: I replaced non-code-compliant semi-rigid transition ductwork in the attic with 26-gauge hard pipe, securing it properly to the framing. A new roof penetration was created and an Inovate DryerJack was installed to provide a code compliant exhaust exit point. Despite the challenging roof pitch, the installation was completed successfully, resulting in a safe and fully functioning dryer exhaust system.

title: Multi Unit Dryer Vent Service
description: Our technician performed a comprehensive dryer vent cleaning and inspection on a multi-unit residential building in San Francisco. The initial inspection revealed severe lint accumulation throughout the entire vent system, including heavily clogged flex ductwork running from the dryer to the exterior, and significant buildup inside the vent transition box and exhaust cap. The dryer exhaust line was routed through the laundry room wall with semi-rigid ducting that showed substantial debris compaction, and the exterior vent cap was completely blocked with lint and debris, severely restricting airflow. Our technician thoroughly cleaned the entire vent run from the dryer connection through to the exterior termination, removed all compressed lint deposits from inside the transition box and surrounding ductwork, cleared the exterior vent cap, and verified proper airflow and seal integrity. The system was restored to safe operating condition with improved drying efficiency and reduced fire hazard risk for all units served by this shared vent system.

title: Wall Vent Installation and Re-route
description: I addressed improper venting by penetrating the exterior wall and installing a wall vent with a 2158a rated transition duct, allowing the dryer to exhaust outside the garage rather than into the interior space. The washer was relocated within the garage to accommodate the new configuration. The homeowner was satisfied with the corrected venting system.

title: Full Dryer and Duct Cleaning
description: The customer reported excessive moisture during laundry loads. Upon inspection, the technician found the dryer in poor condition and performed a complete service on both the dryer unit and vent system. The dryer was restored to proper working order.

title: Routine maintenance.
description: The lint trap assembly was removed and thoroughly cleaned, including the area beneath the lint tray and fan housing where a significant amount of lint had accumulated. After completing the dryer vent service, the dryer was restored to proper operating condition.

title: Dryer Vent Cleaning
description: A comprehensive dryer vent cleaning and inspection was performed on this San Mateo single-family home, which featured a roof-mounted exterior vent cap with rigid metal ductwork running through the attic to the dryer location. The interior ductwork was found to be heavily laden with lint accumulation and debris throughout the run, restricting airflow and creating a fire hazard. The entire vent line was thoroughly cleaned from the dryer connection through to the exterior termination, removing significant lint buildup and restoring proper ventilation. The roof-mounted vent cap was inspected and confirmed to be functioning properly to prevent back-drafting and pest intrusion.

title: Transition duct installation
description: I removed the deteriorated foil-flex ductwork at this San Francisco residence due to excessive lint accumulation and airflow restriction, then installed a new 2158a fire-rated transition duct to connect the dryer to the wall-mounted vent outlet. The interior wall cavity was cleaned of lint buildup, and the new ductwork was sealed and secured to code-compliant standards. These repairs restored proper venting performance and eliminated the fire hazard created by the compromised original system.

title: New Dryer Vent Installation
description: The customer's existing dryer exhaust system was found to be improperly installed, with a transition duct running through the wall that had collapsed, preventing the dryer from operating correctly. A new exhaust system was installed with a roof penetration to safely vent the dryer through the roof. The system now operates safely and efficiently.

title: Booster Fan Removal
description: The customer's dryer vent system was reconfigured to eliminate the unnecessary booster fan. A proper 2158a transition duct was installed, the dryer was thoroughly cleaned, and the system was reassembled. The dryer now performs as expected without the booster fan and is safe and efficient.

title: Full Dryer Exhaust Replacement
description: A complete exhaust system was installed to replace the existing non-compliant setup that was causing dryer errors. The new system included 26-gauge hard pipe, a 2158A fire-rated transition duct, and a vent termination with bird guard, all meeting current code requirements. The dryer now functions correctly with the properly installed exhaust system.

title: Dryer Vent Installation
description: Our technician Michael inspected the customer's existing dryer exhaust system and identified multiple issues requiring replacement. A new system was installed consisting of 26-gauge hard pipe, a 2158A fire-rated transition duct, and a new wall termination. Upon completion, the customer's dryer was safe, functional, and efficient.

title: Dryer Vent Cleaning and Termination Install
description: This was a full service job, which included a vent repair, vent termination install and a full vent cleaning. When I arrive the customer was complaining about long cycle times. It turns out that they had a collapsed transition duct (the one behind the dryer), the exhaust system was very long > 40' and the vent hood on the exterior was damage. I was able to quickly repair all three issue and get the customer back in a safe and efficient working state.

title: Laundromat Duct Cleaning
description: This was a job we completed In San Carlos, CA. We serviced this property last year and were back for the annual cleaning. If your a Laundromat owner it's imperative to service the ducts at least annually. We also inspected each dryer to ensure cleanliness and functionality. This customer is not good for another year.

title: Laundromat Dryer Cleaning
description: I was called out to clean this dryer in a laundromat and man can I tell you that there was a massive amount of lint in the machine right next to the burner tubes. The owner should consider themselves lucky that this machine did not go up in flames.

title: Full Service Exhaust & Dryer Cleaning
description: Our team recently completed a critical dryer exhaust system repair and upgrade at a residential property in Woodside, CA. What began as a routine inspection quickly revealed multiple issues with the dryer exhaust system, posing significant safety risks, including potential fire hazards due to lint buildup and poor airflow. Through detailed diagnostics, thorough cleaning, and the installation of modern, safety-rated components, we restored the system to full functionality, ensuring the homeowner’s laundry setup is now safe, efficient, and compliant with industry standards. The "Before" photo highlights the severity of the issues: a torn transition duct, disconnected ductwork, and excessive lint buildup on the walls and floor, all of which contributed to a hazardous and inefficient dryer exhaust system. The "After" photo showcases a clean, organized, and safe setup with a properly installed DryerFlex vent, secure ductwork, and a lint-free environment. This project not only resolved immediate safety concerns but also improved the dryer’s performance, reducing drying times and energy consumption for the homeowner. Most importantly, the homeowner now has peace of mind knowing their dryer exhaust system is safe and reliable. If you haven’t had your dryer exhaust system inspected recently, now is the time! A blocked or damaged vent can lead to inefficient drying, higher energy bills, and even fire hazards. Contact a professional to assess your system and ensure it’s operating safely and efficiently—just like we did for this Woodside, CA, homeowner. Stay safe and keep your laundry room running smoothly!

title: Thorough Exhaust System Cleaning
description: I was called because the dryer was taking multiple cycles to dryer. Upon inspection it turns our that the transition duct was too long, which is very common as it hard to get the dryer correctly positioned with a short transition duct without the correct tools. I was able to get a correctly sized 2158a fire rated transition duct install and performed a complete cleaning. Once these items were taken care of the customers dryer functioned as intended

title: Dryer & Dryer Vent Cleaning
description: This customer called because their dryer was not dryer properly. Upon inspection there turned out to be three issues 1. the transition duct was not installed correctly. 2. the actual dryer was a mess 3. the roof termination was incorrect and fill clogged. I was able to address the issues and get the dryer in safe efficient working state.

title: New Route Out of the House
description: This was a fire/code compliance project we took on recently in San Mateo, CA. The home purchased a new dryer and upon delivery the dryer would not fit correctly into the existing space. I was not that the dryer was too large but rather the dryer exhaust system was not setup for the space correctly. What was needed in order to correct this situation was the installation of a wall box, which allows more space for the dryer to fit correctly and safely. The main solution that I see in tight spaces is actually a very unsafe once, usually there is a transition duct that looks like a giant slinky, installers use these because they are easy. That said they are 100% incorrect, they are not fore rated and the collapse and tear over time. In order to get our customer up and running we installed the following, A WallBox from InOvate, 12 feet of new 26 Ga hard pipe four inched in diameter a new InOvate DryerWall vent and a UL2158a rate transition duct, which now fits correctly due to the wall box installation.

description: This was a fire/code compliance project we took on recently in San Mateo, CA. The home purchased a new dryer and upon delivery the dryer would not fit correctly into the existing space. title: New Dryer Exhaust Installation
description: This was a fun job that I took on In San Mateo, CA. The customer has an HVAC company install a dryer exhaust system for them and it did not turn out the way it should have in fact the whole setup was incorrect and a hazard. I came up with a simple solution for the customer, which was to re-route the dryer exhaust through the side of the house. The first step was to remove the existing failing dryer exhaust. Once completed I decided to go through the tile floor, this allowed me to reduce the number of turns in the line. Once the floor penetration was completed, I created and exterior penetration to exit the exhaust. You can see form the picture that the penetrations are very clean, that's because we use the correct tools in this case a diamond based core bit. At this point I installed the duct work 8' of 26 GA 4" diameter hard pipe and strapped it to the floor joists to ensure that it would not shift. I finished the run off with a vent hood from a company called InOvate to ensure a sleek look and that no critters would enter the exhaust. I also finished the inside with fire rated caulking on the floor and silicone on the exterior to prevent leaks. The customer now has an efficient, safe and code compliant exhaust system.

title: MagVent Installation
description: I was called out to see if I could get this customer need a little more room in his garage. I came up with a solution that required a new wall penetration and the installation of a MagVent. Once I completed the work the customer received an additional foot of clearance and a much more efficient dryer exhaust. These are some of my favorite jobs to do.

title: New Vent Termination
description: I was called out to this home to do a dimple dryer vent cleaning. I turned out that the exhaust system had several issues. 1. the vent was fully clogged 2. the transition duct was damage 3. the wall termination was not functioning correctly. Was able to take care of all three issue and the customer now has a safe and efficient dryer exhaust system.

title: New Roof Penetration
description: I was called out this house because the dryer was not working correctly. Upon inspection a majority if the duct work was incorrect, I wan able to correct the issues and get the dryer working correctly. This job required that a new roof penetration was needed to get the dryer to exhaust correctly. In addition, the previous installer had used a rectangle duct which was buried in the wall. I was able to install a transition in the attic from rectangle to round and create a new roof penetration, the dryer is now working as it should.

title: First Cleaning in 27 Years!
description: I was called out to this customer’s house for a standard residential dryer vent cleaning upon speaking to the homeowner. It turns out the vent has never been cleaned, which is 27 years. It was unbelievable. The amount of lint in this vent two air whips a rod run from both sides. A new transition duct installed behind the dryer and the dryer is now in good safe operational shape.

title: Booster Fan Repair & Vent Cleaning
description: Customer called me our for a standard dryer vent cleaning. It turns out they had a booster fan removed and the removal was not correctly. I was able to correctly repair the previous job. This job called for hard pipe and not flexible material. Once I made the duct repair I performed a full vent cleaning and got the dryer back in a good safe working order

title: Residential Dryer Vent Cleaning
description: This was a dryer vent that had not been serviced in many years. When I arrive the I found that the pest control company had installed a screen over the termination. This was completely blocking the airflow. I removed the screen and fully serviced the vent. The customer is now in good shape.

title: Dryer Exhaust Re-route
description: I was called out by this customer over concerns of the length of the dryer exhaust system upon inspection. I came up with a solution to dramatically reduce the length of the run. I used long sweep elbows from innovate once I removed the excess length of reassembled the duct system and the dryer is not working as it should.
